notes:
I couldn't write these notes this time. The research tool refused every request, saying I had no calls left for this turn, so I never opened a single page. That includes Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary), Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes and New Advent.

Your rules say to report only what the sources say, cite a URL for every point and leave out what I couldn't find. With nothing retrieved, all of verses 1–8 would be left out. I haven't filled the gap from memory, because those notes would have no sources behind them.

If you send the request again in a new message, the tool may work again. I'd start with these pages:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-129/, biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/129.htm, …/ellicott/psalms/129.htm, …/pulpit/psalms/129.htm, and the Psalm 129 commentary page on preceptaustin.org
- **Baptist:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on Psalm 129, through spurgeon.org or the copies on studylight.org/blueletterbible.org
- **Methodist:** Wesley's notes on Psalm 129 at wesley.nnu.edu
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes on Psalm 129
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org. The Latin Bible numbers the Psalms differently, so Augustine's "Psalm 128" is our Psalm 129.

Verses 5–8 are prayers against Zion's enemies, so they're where I'd most expect traditions to differ. If the sources do differ there, I'll write that up as its own section.
